topics.name: Functions and their properties
topics.summary: A function assigns exactly one output to each input, and its domain, range, monotonicity, and even or odd symmetry describe its behaviour.

topics.name: Linear and quadratic functions
topics.summary: Linear functions f(x)=ax+b have constant slope, and quadratic functions ax²+bx+c form parabolas with a vertex at x=-b/(2a).

topics.name: Limits and one-sided limits
topics.summary: A limit describes the value a function approaches as x nears a point, including one-sided limits and limits that are infinite or involve asymptotes.

topics.name: Continuity
topics.summary: A function is continuous at a point when it is defined there, its limit exists, and the limit equals the function value, with discontinuities classified by type.

topics.name: Limit laws and indeterminate forms
topics.summary: Limit laws combine limits of sums, quotients and products, and indeterminate forms such as 0/0 are resolved by factoring, dividing by the highest power, rationalising, or combining fractions.

topics.name: Trigonometric limits and the squeeze theorem
topics.summary: The squeeze theorem gives lim sin(x)/x = 1 at 0, which yields equivalent-function substitutions for trigonometric limits.

topics.name: Derivative at a point and rate of change
topics.summary: The derivative at a point is the limit of the difference quotient, interpreted as an instantaneous rate of change, velocity, and the slope of the tangent line.

topics.name: Differentiability and higher-order derivatives
topics.summary: A function is differentiable at a point when that limit exists, which requires continuity there but is not guaranteed by it, and higher-order derivatives describe rates of change of the derivative such as acceleration.

topics.name: Basic differentiation rules
topics.summary: The constant rule, power rule, derivatives of sine and cosine, and the linearity rule allow differentiation of sums and constant multiples of basic functions.

topics.name: Product and quotient rules
topics.summary: The product rule differentiates a product of two differentiable functions, and the quotient rule differentiates a ratio where the denominator is nonzero.

topics.name: Chain rule
topics.summary: The chain rule differentiates a composite function by multiplying the derivative of the outer function at the inner function by the derivative of the inner function.
